slides.texte_overlay:
habits that will make you
unreasonably confident

the protected hour

block the first hour of your day for yourself, every single day, and don't give it away. people who protect their time end up being treated like their time matters.

leaving on time

leave work or class on time three days a week, without apologising. staying late to look busy teaches everyone, including you, that your evenings don't count.

two plans a day

never book more than two plans in one day for a month. an overbooked week makes you late, tired and sorry, and none of those ever look like confidence.

five minute mornings

spend 5 minutes of your protected hour learning something: a moment in history, a famous artwork, how the brain works. starting the day curious beats starting it anxious.

five minute mornings

spend 5 minutes of your protected hour learning something: a moment in history, a famous artwork. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and curious mornings beat anxious ones.

slides.texte_overlay:
ending calls on time

when a call or meeting reaches its time, say "i have to stop here" and actually stop. ending things on schedule is a tiny act of self respect that people always notice.
